name: scope-detector-v3-nearmiss
declared: 2026-10-08, before any detector ran on the near-miss rows
purpose: Attack scope-detector v3. Its rule clears inherited codes when at least half of a subtype title's content words appear in the question. Near-miss questions share a word with the title without identifying the subtype. Under-flagging (letting a scope-bound passage through as established) is the dangerous direction, so it is thresholded.

near_miss_set.rows: 12, all labelled unscoped by Claude, written after reading the v3 rule so adversarial by design, not independent

thresholds.N1: v3 clears (fails to flag) at most 3 of the 12 near-miss rows
thresholds.N2: v2 flags all 12 near-miss rows (v2 is the conservative baseline; if it does not, the labels are suspect)

reported_not_thresholded.sweep: Operating points of the subtype rule over share in {0.34, 0.5, 0.67, 1.0} and minimum hits in {1, 2}: for each, scoped-set false flags (of 12), unscoped-set flags (of 12) and near-miss clears (of 12). Choosing a point after seeing both sets is tuning on the same labels and is said to be so.
reported_not_thresholded.E16_and_dev: E16 cleared or not, and development flags, at each operating point

decision_rule: If N1 and N2 hold, v3 is adopted as the candidate detector. If N1 fails, v3 is not adopted as is: the next version must be chosen from the sweep, declared as v4 with its own labels, and labelled as selected on seen data.
limits: Near-miss rows were written to defeat the rule I had just written
N02 (recurring) is ambiguous between two sibling subtypes; I labelled it unscoped because the question does not say which
